plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it's weakly optimal regardless of what others bid. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth if others bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $32, I should bid exactly $32 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so there's no benefit to bidding above or below my true value of $6. Bidding exactly $6 ensures I win whenever the item is worth more to me than what I'd pay, and I never overpay since the price is determined by the second-highest bid, not mine.

Bidding exactly my value ensures I only win when profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. With no prior history to inform deviation, I'll bid my true value of $17.
